title: Shankar Pokharel tells PM Shah to raise border dispute during India visit - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Shankar Pokharel tells PM Shah to raise border dispute during India visit  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Shankar Pokharel

Kathmandu, November 16

CPN-UML General Secretary Shankar Pokharel has urged Prime Minister Balendra Shah to clearly present Nepal’s position on the Nepal-India border dispute during his upcoming visit to India.

Pokharel said the prime minister should correct through his actions what he described as objectionable remarks on issues related to Nepal’s sovereignty and territorial rights.

Speaking at a press conference organised at the party’s central office in Chyasal on Monday, Pokharel recalled that Parliament and political parties had already expressed objections to the prime minister’s remarks on the border dispute.

He accused Shah of correcting only one aspect of his earlier statement, which suggested involving a third party in resolving the dispute, while leaving unaddressed what Pokharel called controversial remarks concerning Nepal’s sovereignty and territorial rights.

Stating that the border issues between Nepal and India had already been documented by both sides, Pokharel said the dispute was a matter of direct concern to Nepal. He argued that the prime minister should firmly defend Nepal’s position rather than make statements that could weaken the country’s claims.

Pokharel said resolving the border dispute should be among the priorities of Shah’s upcoming India visit.

Referring to the map of Greater Nepal that Shah had displayed in his office in the past, Pokharel said the government’s immediate responsibility was to protect Nepal’s existing borders.

“The Nepal-India border issue is documented in the records of both countries. The government must firmly defend Nepal’s position in resolving it. We expect the prime minister to give priority to the border dispute during his upcoming visit to India,” Pokharel said.

He added that while the idea of Greater Nepal was linked to history, the government’s responsibility was to safeguard the country’s present boundaries.

Pokharel also criticised the prime minister’s political working style, saying a leader who had stopped communicating with his own party could hardly be expected to engage in dialogue with opposition parties.

Describing Shah’s approach as undemocratic, arbitrary and authoritarian, Pokharel said dialogue and cooperation with political parties were essential in a democratic system. He urged the prime minister to change his approach.

“Parliament and political parties have already objected to the prime minister’s remarks on the border dispute. Although he corrected his statement regarding the involvement of a third party, he has not corrected the controversial remarks concerning Nepal’s sovereignty and territorial rights,” Pokharel said.

He further said the prime minister’s political conduct did not reflect a democratic and dialogue-oriented approach, urging him to change what he described as an arbitrary and authoritarian style of governance.

title: Nepal retains BB- sovereign credit rating for third consecutive year - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Nepal retains BB- sovereign credit rating for third consecutive year  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
Ministry of Finance

Kathmandu, November 16

Nepal has retained its sovereign credit rating at ‘BB-’ for the third consecutive year, according to the latest assessment by Fitch Ratings.

Under Fitch’s Sovereign Rating Model (SRM), Nepal once again received a BB- rating. The Ministry of Finance said the country’s score increased by 0.19 points to 3.66 this year, up from 3.47 last year.

Last year, Nepal received a BB- rating after an additional notch was awarded through qualitative assessment, despite its underlying score.

This year, however, Nepal secured the BB- rating based entirely on its own score, without any additional qualitative adjustment, the ministry said.

Fitch Ratings has maintained Nepal’s sovereign credit rating at BB- with a stable outlook for the third consecutive year.

The ministry said the rating was achieved despite the adverse circumstances created by devastating floods in Rasuwa, Budhigandaki and other areas. It attributed the assessment to the government’s governance initiatives and broader economic reform programmes.

title: Closure of Tatopani and Rasuwagadhi border points pushes up Nepal-China trade costs - OnlineKhabar English News
description: Closure of Tatopani and Rasuwagadhi border points pushes up Nepal-China trade costs  OnlineKhabar English News
publisher.title: OnlineKhabar English News
full_article:
File: Tatopani border point between Nepal and China

Kathmandu, November 16

Nepal’s two major trade points with China, Tatopani and Rasuwagadhi, are currently out of operation, forcing traders to rely increasingly on the Korala border point in Mustang.

While the Rasuwagadhi crossing has been disrupted by flooding in the Bhotekoshi River, China has also suspended regular commercial movement through Tatopani. As a result, the pressure of Nepal-China trade has shifted towards Korala, where the longer transportation route has significantly increased costs.

The higher freight expenses are putting upward pressure on market prices, while businesses and residents in the Tatopani border area are also losing their livelihoods.

China suspended commercial operations at Tatopani on 14 Bhadra 2083, citing landslide and flood risks along the Araniko Highway. Although the crossing was briefly reopened for three days during the Dashain festival, it was shut again afterwards, bringing business activities in the border area almost to a standstill.

Hotels, shops, transport operators and workers who depend on cross-border trade have been particularly affected.

Trade has faced further disruption following the closure of Rasuwagadhi due to flooding in the Bhotekoshi River. With both major crossings closed, traders have increasingly turned to Korala in Mustang to import goods. However, transporting cargo through this route has proved considerably more expensive.

Businessman Basanta Nepal said transporting a container to Kathmandu costs around Rs 60,000 through Tatopani or Rasuwagadhi, but the expense can reach as much as Rs 600,000 when using the Korala route.

The higher cost is partly due to the distance involved. Goods transported through Korala have to travel around 900 kilometres from Lhasa and another 450 kilometres from Lo Manthang.

The increased freight costs have directly affected the prices of imported goods. Businessman Naniram Tiwari said consumers are now having to pay more as traders pass on the additional transportation expenses.

Traders call for diplomatic efforts to reopen Tatopani

Traders have urged the government to intensify diplomatic efforts to resume operations at Tatopani as soon as possible. They say the federal government’s high-level engagement has so far been insufficient, although dialogue with China is reportedly taking place at the political level.

Madhav Sapkota, a former member of the House of Representatives from Sindhupalchok, and Dr Rupak Sapkota, a foreign policy expert and former foreign affairs adviser to then prime minister Pushpa Kamal Dahal, have held meetings with Chinese political leaders, urging them to fully reopen the border point.

According to former lawmaker Sapkota, the Chinese side has taken the issue seriously and expressed a positive position on reopening the crossing.

However, the issue extends beyond traders’ demands for the resumption of business. China has prioritised border security in view of the Bhotekoshi floods, the possibility of glacial lake outburst floods and landslide risks near the crossing.

Stakeholders say the government must complement diplomatic dialogue with investments in safer roads, reliable early warning systems and infrastructure to reduce disaster risks if Nepal-China trade is to operate smoothly.

title: NASC signs Nepal scaffolding skills agreement - Scaffmag
description: NASC signs Nepal scaffolding skills agreement  Scaffmag
publisher.title: Scaffmag
full_article:
NASC has signed an agreement with Nepal’s Scaffolders Association to develop cooperation on scaffolding training and safety.

The memorandum of understanding was announced today (16 November), following its signing on 26 October by Clive Dickin, group chief executive of NASC and CISRS, and the association’s founding president Dipak Prasad Uprety.

The two bodies will share knowledge on scaffolding education, competence assessment and industry standards. Equipment testing requirements and safe working practices are also covered.

They will explore joint work on instructor development, refresher training, continuing professional development and research, alongside links with government authorities and vocational education institutions in Nepal.

The joint announcement points to Nepal’s contribution to the international scaffolding workforce, particularly in Gulf Cooperation Council countries.

Practical initiatives will be agreed through further discussions between the organisations.

The Nepal-based association’s wider plans include developing scaffolding curricula and seeking recognition from relevant industry bodies. It also wants to establish training centres across Nepal’s seven provinces over time.

The agreement follows a separate NASC memorandum with the Korean Temporary Equipment & Engineering Association, signed at ScaffEx26 in Manchester.

That arrangement covers sharing expertise and best practice, building on the two bodies’ involvement in the International Access and Scaffolding Association.
